description: Offence keys printed with 4 digits until 2007 and 6 digits from 2008 (2200 becomes 220000). Mapped one to one in offence_map.csv.
evidence: Group legends of the PDF tables name the same offence groups in 2007 and 2008

description: The second PDF offence column changes from bodily harm (220000) to dangerous and serious bodily harm (222000). Separate keys, never linked (BUG-011, BUG-013).
evidence: PDF headers 2009 and 2010; 2013 publishes both: 220000 = 533,432 and 222000 = 127,833 nationally

description: Case counts are published from 2013 (Excel). For 2003 to 2012 counts are cases_derived = hz * population / 1e5 from rounded HZ (BUG-015).
evidence: National ------: 5,947,383 derived for 2012, 5,910,911 published for 2013. Derived district sums fall short of the national yearbook total by the same share as published district sums (cases with unknown place): ------ -0.83 percent in 2012 against -0.85 percent in 2013, 222000 -0.02 against -0.03, 435*00 +0.01 against 0.00, *50*00 -0.16 against -0.18, 674000 -0.57 against -0.58. Recomputing 2013 to 2025 from integer HZ: national totals within 0.001 percent, cells with 100 or more cases within 0.56 percent (p95), cells under 10 cases off by 7.3 percent (median)

description: HZ denominator based on Zensus 2011 (header: HZ nach Zensus 2011); PDF years use the population update of 1 January (BUG-026). The HZ of year t refers to the population of 31.12.(t - 1). Compare counts, or recompute rates on one census base with pksR::pks_rates(population = "corrected"), which uses the census-corrected population of the BBSR (column population_corrected).
evidence: Excel header 2013 (HZ nach Zensus 2011); PDF tables use Einwohner am 01.01. of the reporting year (2009: 01.01.09, 2012: 01.01.2012), before the census revision. The federal PKS 2013 report notes that the Zensus-based population (01.01.2013) deviates from the earlier update

description: HZ denominator based on Zensus 2022 (header: HZ nach Zensus 2022) (BUG-026). As for BRK-004, pksR::pks_rates(population = "corrected") puts all years on one census base.
evidence: Excel header 2024 (HZ nach Zensus 2022); the 2023 table still divides by the Zensus 2011 based population of 31.12.2022

description: 890000 is published from 2015; for 2014 it is computed as ------ minus 725000 (suspects NA), as decided by the maintainer (question Q4 of the offence review).
evidence: Identity exact for cases, attempts and cleared in all 4,409 district rows 2015 to 2025

description: Three scopes in one key: 2014 to 2016 para. 177 Abs. 2 to 4 and 178 StGB; 2017 para. 177 Abs. 1 to 4 and 6 to 9 and 178 StGB after the reform of the sexual offences law (in force 10 November 2016, first full PKS year 2017); from 2018 only especially serious cases incl. resulting in death. A second break follows in 2018.

Labels add para. 244a StGB in 2016 and para. 244 Abs. 4 StGB from 2018. The cited paragraphs change, the offence described does not; the national series shows the known decline without a step at either year.

621020 and 621021 (until 2017) are replaced by 621100, 621110 and 621120 (paras. 113 to 115 StGB) from 2018. Para. 114 StGB (assault on enforcement officers) is in force since 30 May 2017; PKS 2017 still counts such assaults in the old keys. Not linked: assaults counted in 621020 move to the new 621120.

Fraud label adds paras. 265c to 265e StGB (sports betting fraud and match fixing, new offences of 2017) in 2018. The added offences are negligible, so the drop in 2018 is not caused by the label change.
evidence: Published labels 2017 and 2018; national 854,435 (2017), 778,537 (2018); Bund table 518500 (paras. 265c to 265e StGB): 3 (2018), 5 (2019)

description: Label adds killing on request (para. 216 StGB) in 2016, but the key included it before: in the Bund table 892500 equals 010000 (murder) plus 020000 (manslaughter and killing on request, paras. 212, 213, 216 StGB) in every year from 2013. The rise in 2016 is in murder and manslaughter, not a recording change.

Summary key renamed from Computerkriminalitaet to Cybercrime with effect from 1 January 2021; it no longer includes software piracy (715100, 715200), so the police call it not directly comparable with earlier years. 980100 is closed for recording and leaves both the Bund and the Kreis table.
evidence: Bayerisches Landeskriminalamt, Lagebild Cybercrime Bayern 2021, p. 7; Bund table 2020: 897000 = 130,611, software piracy 715100 + 715200 = 134 (0.10 percent); district sums 102,506 (2020), 114,702 (2021)

description: Some years are published on the previous year's boundary after mid-year reforms: 2008 on 2007, 2009 on 2008, 2011 on 2010, 2016 on 2015, 2021 on 2020. Harmonization starts from the published boundary (registry/sources.csv, boundary_year).
evidence: District sets per year match the BBSR crosswalk at that boundary (audit section 4)

description: Theft in/from motor vehicles (in/aus, until 2011) becomes theft of parts from and items out of motor vehicles (an/aus) in 2012. The BKA yearbook 2012 prints (-) instead of a change against 2011, i.e. not comparable.
evidence: Yearbook 2011: 242,563; yearbook 2012: 343,460 with (-); district sums 242,298 and 342,908

description: Cannabis Act (KCanG) in force from 1 April 2024: most cannabis possession offences no longer count as drug offences. 2024 is a partial year under the new law, 2025 the first full year. The totals ------ and 890000 lose the same cases: their decline from 2023 to 2024 is smaller than the drop in 730000 alone. From 2024, 730000 includes the remaining offences under para. 34 KCanG (736000) and para. 25 MedCanG (737000).

The list of component keys disappears from the label of 980100 in 2016 and its national count doubles; renamed Cybercrime im engeren Sinne in 2017 without a further step. The step carries over to the parent 897000: 897000 without 980100 stays between 21,852 and 24,906 from 2014 to 2020.
